TELLUX, a French start-up, is the result of 10 years of research by dynamic researchers of INSA and University of Rouen Normandy, France. The name ​TELLUX, blend of ​Tellus (Earth in Latin) and ​Lux (Light in Latin)​, is a great synopsis of the activity of our Young Innovative Company (JEI status in France), which fulfills a promise that is both ambitious and highly technical: to analyze and measure the concentration of pollutants soil by means of hyperspectral imagery, and then to provide detailed reports. 
The striking force of TELLUX is a R&D team of ​three researchers, all PhD-holders, with complementary expertise in Informatics (Machine Learning) and Chemistry (analytical chemistry), with application to spectroscopy and hyperspectral imagery:
- Antonin Van Exem ​is a geoscientist researcher, working on visible spectroscopy (VIS) since 2009. He defended his PhD thesis in 2018 on hyperspectral imagery for sedimentology.
- Paul Honeine is a Professor at University of Rouen. He has been working on Machine Learning since 2003, and on hyperspectral data since 2010. He has published about 200 research papers in Machine Learning, including 1/4 on hyperspectral imagery.
- Mélanie Mignot is an Assistant Professor at INSA Rouen Normandy. She is expert in analytical methodologies, such as microcolumn chromatography. She has been involved in several European collaborations, including Pharmaceutical Chemical Analysis Laboratory (Geneva), and Organic Chemistry Laboratory (Brussels). She was also the laureate of the European Project ChromaFish. She has published more than 25 papers in international journals and conferences, receiving two best scientific presentation awards.

CIHEAM IAMC is the 4th constituent institute of CIHEAM, the International Centre for Advanced Mediterranean Agronomic Studies, an Intergovernmental Organisation which was founded at the joint initiative of the OECD and the Council of Europe on 21 May 1962 under an agreement signed by the governments of seven southern European countries: France, Greece, Italy, Portugal, Spain, Turkey and Yugoslavia.
The 1962 agreement establishing the Centre stipulates that CIHEAM's mission consists in "providing supplementary education (economic as well as technical) and developing a spirit of international cooperation among agricultural personnel in Mediterranean countries". According to article 15 of this agreement, every country on the Mediterranean rim is potentially eligible for membership of CIHEAM.In the mid nineteen-eighties CIHEAM therefore began to open up to countries on the southern and eastern shores of the Mediterranean Basin. This initiative resulted in the accession of several new Member States: Tunisia (1985), Egypt and Algeria (1986), Malta (1989), Morocco (1991), Albania (1992) and Lebanon (1994).
CIHEAM is made up of four Mediterranean Agronomic Institutes (MAIs), located in Bari (Italy), Chania (Greece), Montpellier (France) and Zaragoza (Spain), and a General Secretariat based in Paris.
Since 1986, and as the 4th constituent institute of CIHEAM, IAMC pursues its three main complementary missions through
- post-graduate specialised education
- networked research
- facilitation of regional debate
with focus in the fields of Business Economics and Management, Geoinformation in Environmental Management, Horticultural Genetics and Biotechnology, Food Quality and Chemistry of Natural Products, Sustainable Agriculture, and has established itself as an authority in Mediterranean agriculture, Food and Rural Development.
In particular the Department of Geoinformation in Environmental Management has been employing EO data for over 20 years, on applications as agriculture, forestry and natural vegetation monitoring. These activities are undertaken both in the framework of education, as well as research, by participating in EU-funded projects since the late 1990s.

entityDescription:
Technoport is a technology business incubator that was launched back in June 1998 as a department of the Public Research Centre Henri Tudor[1]. In 2012 the incubator span-out of the research centre and merged with another public initiative supporting startups as well as foreign innovative companies establishing research and development centres in Luxembourg. 
Since 2012 the new Technoport is a limited company owned by two shareholders – the Ministry of the Economy (55%) and a public bank, the SNCI (www.snci.lu) (45%). The incubator runs 5 different facilities on two geographical sites representing a combined surface of over 16.000 sqm. It has a great mix of office and industrial spaces. 
The incubator is a generic incubator open to all kind of sectors. Within the 40 companies that it hosts in average at a given moment you can find a great mix between ICT, software, space, environment, material science, IoT and/or health tech companies. This mix has proven to be a great added-value in the past to create unexpected synergies and a good exchange among entrepreneurs. 
Mission and activities
Technopot’s core activity is to support entrepreneurs in the validation, creation and development of technology companies through a flexible, but thorough, staged selection process which accepts in average between 7-10% of the overall annual deal-flow into the final official incubation program[2]. 
The incubator targets also foreign companies that decide to establish a research and development centre in Luxembourg with a flexible ramp-up support scheme by hosting them during an initial settlement period. 
On top of that the incubator has also a soft-landing support scheme for foreign startup companies that are in an internationalisation process. 
Last but not least Technoport has established a joint venture with Vodafone Procurement Company called Tomorrow Street (www.tomorrowstreet.co). It is an innovation centre that accelerates leading edge technology through scaling late stage startups. The center hosts and supports the next generation of strategic suppliers to Vodafone, and is a technology hub that attracts entrepreneurs and talent to the fast growing tech sector in Luxembourg.
Over the years the incubator has built strong networks with different types of partners (investors, corporates, mentors, coaches, research centres, regulators, …) that support its environment. 
As of 31.07.2020 the incubator has accepted a total of 157 companies throughout the years
79 left the incubator with success after an average hosting period of 3.3 years. 
Among those that left 18 got acquired by foreign companies. 
[1] Today part of the Luxembourg Institute of Science and Technology (www.list.lu). 
[2] The selection process can be found in the download section on www.technoport.lu

entityDescription:
Cesam Seed is an IT consulting and services provider in specific field called PLM : Product Lifecycle Management

Many companies have embraced PLM as a way of using software to manage a product from the dawn to dusk of its life.
PLM systems help organizations in coping with the increasing complexity and engineering challenges of developing new products for the global competitive markets. PLM describes the engineering aspect of a product, from managing descriptions and properties of a product through its development and useful life.
Product lifecycle management can be considered one of the four cornerstones of a manufacturing corporation's information technology structure. All companies need to manage communications and information with their customers (CRM-customer relationship management), their suppliers and fulfillment (SCM-supply chain management), their resources within the enterprise (ERP-enterprise resource planning) and their product planning and development (PLM).

Within PLM there are five primary areas; 
- Systems engineering (SE) is focused on meeting all requirements, primarily meeting customer needs, and coordinating the systems design process by involving all relevant disciplines. An important aspect for life cycle management is a subset within Systems Engineering called Reliability Engineering.
- Product and portfolio m² (PPM) is focused on managing resource allocation, tracking progress, plan for new product development projects that are in process (or in a holding status). Portfolio management is a tool that assists management in tracking progress on new products and making trade-off decisions when allocating scarce resources.
- Product design (CAx) is the process of creating a new product to be sold by a business to its customers.
- Manufacturing process management (MPM) is a collection of technologies and methods used to define how products are to be manufactured.
- Product data management (PDM) is focused on capturing and maintaining information on products and/or services through their development and useful life. Change management is an important part of PDM/PLM.

UniDoc S.r.l. (following UniDoc) is a spin-off from the University of Salerno formed in October 2017. Its mission is the technology transfer activities focused on engineering research results in well-identified market sectors (such as digitization of public administration (PA) particularly in the healthcare sector). After the establishment, it was registered as an innovative start-up. It was naturally a candidate as a technology enabler for PA's innovation processes.
Capitalizing on skills and experiences of the founders, today it offers to the market, in partnership with large companies, technological solutions to promote the digitization process of the PA making it more effective. In particular, in partnership with the CSA consortium, it has been able to manage a huge amount of information obtained from the digitization of millions of hospital medical records. The enhancement of this heritage, in all the clinical/administrative processes of hospital companies, has focused almost 80% of the resources and activities of the spin-off. The huge amount (dozens of TB) and the specificity of the data processed in addition to their intrinsic value required conscious use of the technologies. 
With a set of Big Data tools specifically designed to deal with large amounts of data, unexpected knowledge was extracted, studying phenomena still unknown (of particular interest to pharmaceutical companies). 
In this extremely sensitive area, such as medical records, UniDoc has developed a flexible and reliable infrastructure to afford the topic of Big Data Analytics. All the analysis procedures are fed by well-known and (and therefore still widely used) data sources such as paper-based medical records after a robust process to appropriately digitize, normalize and qualify the output.
